requirements.quote: Provide a searchable register for 1,800 assets across three plants and import up to 5,000 CSV rows in one format, preserving asset identifiers and reporting rejected rows.
Generate work orders from calendar-based recurring maintenance plans, assign an owner and due date, and record completion notes; meter-based or predictive scheduling is excluded.
Use the existing LDAP directory for authentication without writing to it; technicians access only their own plant and central planners access all plants, enforced by the application service.

Synchronize completed-work history daily from the existing PostgreSQL database through a read-only connector; do not migrate, alter, or write to that database, although a separate application database is permitted.
Supply printable work-order PDFs and a responsive browser interface; native mobile apps and offline two-way synchronization are outside the first release.
Complete an Essen pilot with ten technicians for three consecutive weeks before deploying to Kassel or Ulm, using a documented export-based rollback to existing planning within one working day.

Include 12 months of support after full go-live, Monday–Friday 07:00–17:00 Europe/Berlin excluding German public holidays; acknowledge critical outages within four coverage hours and other issues within two business days.

Acceptance requires all 40 agreed scheduling and access-control tests to pass, a reconciliation of imported/rejected rows and asset identifiers, and a demonstrated daily history refresh within 24 hours; provide administrator instructions and three remote plant training sessions.

Quote an itemized fixed total of €90,000–€125,000 excluding VAT for implementation and all hosting, licenses, and support during the first 12 months after full go-live, with explicitly priced assumptions.

Begin the working Essen pilot by the start of week 10 and complete rollout to all three plants by the end of week 18 from kickoff, with the full three-week pilot completed before either other plant launches.

findings.rfp_quote: Synchronize completed-work history daily from the existing PostgreSQL database through a read-only connector; do not migrate, alter, or write to that database, although a separate application database is permitted.
findings.response_quote: We will not migrate, alter, or write to the existing PostgreSQL database.
findings.rationale: The proposal preserves the source and specifies a daily read-only connector and separate application database.

findings.rfp_quote: Complete an Essen pilot with ten technicians for three consecutive weeks before deploying to Kassel or Ulm, using a documented export-based rollback to existing planning within one working day.
findings.response_quote: The ten-technician Essen pilot starts at the beginning of week 10 and runs for three consecutive weeks through the end of week 12.
findings.rationale: Pilot size, duration, sequence, and deadlines align with the RFP.

findings.rfp_quote: Quote an itemized fixed total of €90,000–€125,000 excluding VAT for implementation and all hosting, licenses, and support during the first 12 months after full go-live, with explicitly priced assumptions.
findings.rationale: The six fixed items total €112,000 and include 12 months of all stated operating costs.

findings.rfp_quote: Synchronize completed-work history daily from the existing PostgreSQL database through a read-only connector; do not migrate, alter, or write to that database, although a separate application database is permitted.
findings.response_quote: A stable record identifier and update timestamp must be confirmed in week 1; if unavailable, we will agree a read-only full-refresh method and validate capacity before pilot entry.
findings.rationale: The uninspected source is acknowledged and a compatible fallback is planned.

notes: New completion notes stay in the application database; this does not violate the prohibition on writes to legacy PostgreSQL.
A daily-refresh failure notification makes stale data visible without promising zero failures.

findings.rfp_quote: Synchronize completed-work history daily from the existing PostgreSQL database through a read-only connector; do not migrate, alter, or write to that database, although a separate application database is permitted.
findings.response_quote: For simpler operations, we will migrate the existing PostgreSQL history into our hosted database and replace the legacy instance at launch.
findings.rationale: The mandatory architecture expressly migrates and replaces a system the RFP requires preserving.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep PostgreSQL unchanged and implement the requested daily read-only history connector.

findings.rfp_quote: Supply printable work-order PDFs and a responsive browser interface; native mobile apps and offline two-way synchronization are outside the first release.
findings.response_quote: The first release includes native technician apps with offline two-way synchronization and meter-based predictive scheduling.
findings.rationale: The mandatory first-release additions contradict both excluded scheduling modes and mobile/offline boundaries.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove these additions from the first release and price any future options separately.

findings.rfp_quote: Generate work orders from calendar-based recurring maintenance plans, assign an owner and due date, and record completion notes; meter-based or predictive scheduling is excluded.
findings.response_quote: Our prediction engine guarantees elimination of every unplanned equipment outage from the launch date, even without prior machine telemetry.
findings.rationale: A scheduling proposal has no supplied evidence or operational control supporting elimination of equipment failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the universal outcome guarantee and define measurable software acceptance criteria.

findings.rfp_quote: Quote an itemized fixed total of €90,000–€125,000 excluding VAT for implementation and all hosting, licenses, and support during the first 12 months after full go-live, with explicitly priced assumptions.
findings.response_quote: It also guarantees a 45% reduction in maintenance spend during the first quarter, regardless of asset condition or current service arrangements.
findings.rationale: The cost-saving promise lacks a baseline, measurement method, or defensible assumptions; the quoted project total itself is clear and within budget.
findings.suggested_fix: State any savings as a hypothesis with a baseline and evaluation method, not an unconditional guarantee.

findings.rfp_quote: Begin the working Essen pilot by the start of week 10 and complete rollout to all three plants by the end of week 18 from kickoff, with the full three-week pilot completed before either other plant launches.
findings.response_quote: Our schedule remains guaranteed even if source access is not supplied until the last day of week 4.
findings.rationale: Source migration and mapping are scheduled through week 4, so the unconditional late-access promise lacks a credible contingency.
findings.suggested_fix: State access deadlines, remapping effort, and a change process for schedule impact.

notes: The €118,000 total is within the RFP budget and arithmetically correct.
The three-week pilot and plant rollout sequence satisfy the requested dates. Clear dates are distinct from unsupported confidence in execution.
Current hosted history is not the required daily refresh from existing PostgreSQL, making R8 partial.
Do not force an overall weak-versus-overpromised ranking.

findings.rfp_quote: Provide a searchable register for 1,800 assets across three plants and import up to 5,000 CSV rows in one format, preserving asset identifiers and reporting rejected rows.
findings.response_quote: We will review a sample of the CSV file before agreeing the final import layout and effort.
findings.rationale: The register size is covered, but the 5,000-row allowance, identifier preservation, and rejected-row reporting are not committed.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit to the import limit, preserved identifiers, and rejected-row reconciliation.

findings.rfp_quote: Use the existing LDAP directory for authentication without writing to it; technicians access only their own plant and central planners access all plants, enforced by the application service.
findings.response_quote: Authentication arrangements and the detailed access model will be confirmed with the IT contact at a design workshop.
findings.rationale: LDAP, no directory writes, and service-enforced plant isolation are unconfirmed; the separate history refresh interval is also unresolved.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify LDAP read-only authentication, service-enforced roles, and daily history refresh.

findings.rfp_quote: Begin the working Essen pilot by the start of week 10 and complete rollout to all three plants by the end of week 18 from kickoff, with the full three-week pilot completed before either other plant launches.
findings.response_quote: We will prepare a delivery calendar once access and the first CSV sample have been received; no milestone dates are committed in this offer.
findings.rationale: The proposal has phases but no pilot or full-rollout dates, and the pilot size/duration are deferred.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide a ten-person, three-week Essen pilot starting by week 10 and full deployment by week 18, with rollback.

findings.rfp_quote: Quote an itemized fixed total of €90,000–€125,000 excluding VAT for implementation and all hosting, licenses, and support during the first 12 months after full go-live, with explicitly priced assumptions.
findings.response_quote: Hosting, licenses, and the first-year support package will be priced after discovery, so no all-in total is available yet.
findings.rationale: The implementation subtotal cannot establish compliance with the full first-year budget.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote all operating costs and a fixed total with priced assumptions.

findings.rfp_quote: Include 12 months of support after full go-live, Monday–Friday 07:00–17:00 Europe/Berlin excluding German public holidays; acknowledge critical outages within four coverage hours and other issues within two business days.
findings.response_quote: Issues preventing normal work will be prioritized, with service hours and response commitments agreed in the support contract.
findings.rationale: Service commitments are postponed; the described walkthrough also lacks the required quantified acceptance checks.
findings.suggested_fix: State the full support coverage and acknowledgement terms, plus the 40 tests, import reconciliation, refresh demonstration, and three training sessions.

notes: The scope boundaries for native apps and predictive scheduling are followed.
Preserving the legacy database is explicit; daily refresh frequency remains an omission rather than an explicit contradiction.
A correct implementation subtotal is not a complete all-in first-year price.

findings.rfp_quote: Synchronize completed-work history daily from the existing PostgreSQL database through a read-only connector; do not migrate, alter, or write to that database, although a separate application database is permitted.
findings.response_quote: The source will not be migrated, altered, or written to; new planning records reside in a separate application database.
findings.rationale: The core architecture preserves PostgreSQL and specifies daily read-only synchronization.

findings.rfp_quote: Begin the working Essen pilot by the start of week 10 and complete rollout to all three plants by the end of week 18 from kickoff, with the full three-week pilot completed before either other plant launches.
findings.response_quote: Its calendar dates and the remaining deployment milestones will be agreed with the project owner after discovery.
findings.rationale: The ten-person, three-week pilot sequence is specified, but neither deadline nor timed rollback is committed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a pilot start by week 10, completion by week 18, and a one-working-day rollback procedure.

findings.rfp_quote: Quote an itemized fixed total of €90,000–€125,000 excluding VAT for implementation and all hosting, licenses, and support during the first 12 months after full go-live, with explicitly priced assumptions.
findings.response_quote: The treatment of hosting, licenses, and first-year support in this range has not yet been finalized.
findings.rationale: The indicative price range has uncertain inclusions and no firm breakdown.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote a fixed total including every required first-year cost and state priced assumptions.

findings.rfp_quote: Include 12 months of support after full go-live, Monday–Friday 07:00–17:00 Europe/Berlin excluding German public holidays; acknowledge critical outages within four coverage hours and other issues within two business days.
findings.response_quote: Support hours, acknowledgement targets, and the covered period will be agreed as part of that arrangement.
findings.rationale: The proposal postpones all measurable support commitments.
findings.suggested_fix: State 12 months of support, the requested coverage hours, and acknowledgement targets.

findings.rfp_quote: Acceptance requires all 40 agreed scheduling and access-control tests to pass, a reconciliation of imported/rejected rows and asset identifiers, and a demonstrated daily history refresh within 24 hours; provide administrator instructions and three remote plant training sessions.
findings.response_quote: Acceptance will use scheduling scenarios, plant-permission checks, and a review of imported records.
findings.rationale: Acceptance does not commit to all 40 tests, complete import reconciliation, or a demonstrated refresh within 24 hours.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the stated acceptance counts, reconciliation, and refresh demonstration.

notes: Core features and explicit architecture boundaries are addressed; omissions focus on delivery assurances and commercial completeness.
The correct pilot duration does not establish compliance with calendar deadlines.
